screening_decisions.reason: This study evaluates Arginine Butyrate (a drug) vs standard local care for leg ulcers. No RBC transfusion intervention is tested. The intervention is pharmacological, not transfusion-based.

This RCT directly compares two RBC transfusion strategies (conservative vs aggressive) for preventing perioperative complications in SCD patients. This aligns perfectly with the review objective of comparing restrictive vs liberal transfusion approaches.

This article discusses red cell exchange transfusions as therapy for acute and chronic SCD complications including stroke, acute chest syndrome, and multi-organ failure. As this is an overview of Cochrane reviews, review articles about transfusion therapy are potentially relevant.

This is a general overview article about SCD pathophysiology and clinical management. While it mentions transfusion briefly, it does not evaluate RBC transfusion interventions or their effectiveness/safety.

Similar to study 24, this is a general review article about SCD. It mentions transfusions as one of several treatments but does not focus on evaluating transfusion interventions for specific complications.
This brief article is about epidemiology and migration patterns of SCD. It does not address RBC transfusion interventions at all.
This study focuses on genetic factors affecting SCD phenotype. It does not involve RBC transfusion interventions or evaluate their effectiveness.

This RCT compares no pre-operative transfusion vs simple/partial exchange transfusion in SCD patients undergoing surgery. This directly addresses the review question of transfusion vs no transfusion for preventing perioperative complications.
This landmark RCT compares transfusions (to reduce HbS <30%) vs standard care for preventing first stroke in high-risk children. This is a key study on transfusion for stroke prevention in SCD.

This RCT compares chronic transfusion therapy with chelation vs hydroxyurea with phlebotomy for children with SCA, prior stroke, and iron overload. Transfusion is a key component of the intervention being evaluated.
This observational study identifies LDH as a biomarker for hemolysis-associated complications. It does not test or evaluate RBC transfusion interventions.

This review summarizes transfusion management for neurologic complications, perioperative care, acute chest syndrome, and acute anemia in SCD. As this is an overview of Cochrane reviews, review articles about transfusion therapy are potentially relevant sources.
This RCT evaluates a herbal extract (Cajanus cajan) vs placebo for reducing painful crises. No RBC transfusion intervention is involved.
This RCT compares surgical (core decompression) vs physical therapy for osteonecrosis. No RBC transfusion intervention is tested.
This is a methodological paper about developing a tool for assessing systematic review quality. It has no relevance to SCD or RBC transfusion interventions.

This cross-sectional study examines HIV transmission rates among transfused SCD children. While it relates to transfusion safety, it does not evaluate the effectiveness of RBC transfusions for treating or preventing SCD complications - rather it assesses infection risk from transfusions.
This RCT compares topical treatments (Solcoseryl, DuoDerm, Eusol) for chronic leg ulcers in SCD. No RBC transfusion intervention is involved.
